answer: A reputation spiral breaks Sybil economics: new agents start with zero trust and can only earn standing through completed, peer-attested work, so a raven-like swarm of fresh fake identities cannot borrow credibility. Each verified task adds a little weight, while inactivity and failed attestations erode it, forcing an attacker to keep paying real work costs per identity. A falcon-fast audit then samples high-trust agents for anomalies, and any cluster sharing the same work patterns is quarantined together, so multiplying identities multiplies cost instead of multiplying influence.
